title: Development and Evaluation of School-Based Back Health Education Programs for Realschulen and Gymnasien: "Rückenfit – Our School Takes Part"
summary:
This study investigates whether a four-week school-based back training program can improve posture, spinal mobility, and trunk muscle endurance in children. In addition, it examines whether the program increases children's knowledge of back health and leads to changes in health-related physical activity behavior.
The program consists of educational lessons including practical exercises and simple explanations about back health. Outcomes will be assessed before and after the program using standardized physical tests and questionnaires.
conditions: Back pain and postural abnormalities in children and adolescents, as well as associated functional impairments.

interventions.name:
Participants take part in a four-week school-based back health education program. The program consists of one physical education session and one theoretical lesson per week.
In addition, participants receive exercise cards containing specific exercises to strengthen the abdominal and trunk muscles.
Participants attend regular school lessons over a period of four weeks without an additional back health education program.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
student enrolled in year 5 either at Realschule Riedenburg or at Donaugymnasium Kehlheim
Exclusion criteria:
Acute orthopedic conditions, acute injuries, contraindications to physical exercise, and lack of informed consent from the parents or legal guardians
